docs.title: Welcome to the Coding Agents for Test Workshop
docs.text:
Thank you for joining the UiPath Coding Agents for Test Workshop!

This Learner's Handbook is your hands-on guide for the workshop. We keep the theory short and get you building fast: in one day you'll take a requirement all the way to an automated test run, and finish by asking an AI agent to triage the failures and write a go/no-go release report in plain English.

Before the workshop

Complete the Prerequisites before the session starts. You install Studio and Delegate, and the hands-on steps depend on them.

Your trainer will share the organization and tenant you'll use during the workshop.

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text:
You'll walk through the full testing lifecycle in UiPath Test Cloud, with AI at every step:

Phase 1 · Set up Orchestrator + TM 1Import and link the project Project, linked to your folder Phase 2 · Plan & test Test Manager 2Evaluate requirements 3Generate test cases 4Run manual tests Autopilot for Testers, plus Delegate for manual runs Phase 3 · Build Studio + Delegate 5Build the Object Repository 6Automate and publish Project, Object Repository, automation, test data, and publishing Phase 4 · Run & report TM + Delegate 7Add to the smoke test set 8Run, triage, and report A smoke run → triage → go/no-go PDF

Select a step to jump to it.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this workshop, you will:

✅ Use the agentic features in Test Manager to evaluate requirements and generate test cases

✅ Use Delegate to run manual tests, build the Object Repository, triage failures against the requirement, and write a go/no-go release report

✅ Turn manual test cases into automations with Autopilot for Testers in Studio

docs.title: How this guide is organized
docs.text:
Section What's inside Prerequisites Accounts, Delegate, and installation Introduction A short tour of Test Cloud, Test Manager, and Delegate Hands-On Workshop The eight hands-on steps, from import to the go/no-go report Troubleshooting & Next Steps More prompts to try and fixes for common problems

Here's something worth holding onto as you work through this workshop

AI agents don't replace testers — they give testers a new way to work. Instead of clicking through dashboards to find out what failed and why, you ask a question in plain English and get an answer grounded in your real test data.

Robots bring determinism and control, agents bring adaptability and reasoning. This workshop is about putting the two together.

Next → Prerequisites

docs.title: Trainer Setup
docs.text: Complete this checklist before the workshop, ideally a few days ahead.

docs.title: Organization and tenant
docs.text:
✅ Create the workshop tenant in an organization.

Test Cloud only

Run autonomously and Autonomous Exploration are only available in Test Cloud.

✅ Make sure the tenant has Test Manager, Orchestrator, and Data Fabric enabled.

✅ Make sure Autopilot for Testers is allowed for the tenant, in Test Manager and in Studio. Check that no AI Trust Layer or governance policy blocks it.

Check it

Open a requirement in Test Manager → Optimize Coverage: Evaluate Quality is available.

✅ Make sure learners can use Delegate in the organization.

docs.title: Users and group
docs.text:
✅ Create a group for the workshop.

✅ Invite each learner to the organization, and add them to the group.

✅ Give permissions to the group, not to individual users, so late joiners get everything at once.

docs.title: Licenses and runtimes
docs.text:
Use the column for your organization type.

Test Cloud organization Automation Cloud organization Learner user license App Test Developer - Named User (App Tester can't create or publish Test Automation projects) Automation Developer - Named User (includes Tester for Test Manager) Where to assign Organization-wide, no tenant allocation User license to the group or each learner Robot runtime for the tenant App Test Robot: at least one per learner machine Testing: at least one per learner machine Machine template runtime type App Testing Testing Run autonomously, Autonomous Exploration (step 4 tips) Available Not available

Optional: Run autonomously and Autonomous Exploration

For these tips in step 4, make sure a supported, non-serverless robot is available in each project's default folder. The robot machine must run Windows, and its UiPath browser extension must have Allow in Incognito turned on.

docs.title: Test Manager
docs.text: ✅ Give the group the Project Creator tenant role.

docs.title: Orchestrator
docs.text:
Recommended

Do the Prerequisites folder and robot setup for each learner before the session, so learners don't need tenant-level rights.

✅ For the Prerequisites folder and robot setup, give the group the Orchestrator rights to configure unattended automation settings for their machine using machine domain name and password.

docs.title: Data Fabric
docs.text:
✅ Create the UiBankTestData entity from Schema.json.

✅ Import the test data from UiBankLoanData.csv into the entity.

✅ Give the group the Data Reader role.

docs.title: On the day
docs.text: ✅ Share the organization name and tenant name with learners.

docs.title: After the workshop
docs.text: ✅ Clean up the imported projects, learner folders, the Data Fabric entity, and robot runtime assignments. Remove learners from the group, or delete the tenant.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Use this checklist to confirm you're ready before the workshop starts.

docs.title: Your machine
docs.text:
✅ A Windows 10 or 11 laptop. The workshop uses Studio Desktop, and your machine runs your tests as a robot.

✅ Local admin rights, to install Studio and the UiPath browser extension

✅ A browser: Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge

✅ Screen lock off for the workshop day: set the screen to never turn off and the laptop to never sleep while plugged in. Delegate and your robot need an unlocked screen. Turn it back on afterwards.

✅ UiPath Studio, latest STS version: download and run UiPathPlatformSTS.msi

Install the latest STS version

Delegate is only in Short Term Support (STS) versions of Studio. Install the latest one, even if you already have Studio.

✅ Access to cloud.uipath.com and uibank.uipath.com, with no proxy or firewall blocking them

docs.title: Accounts and access
docs.text:
Access is provided by your trainer

Your trainer gives you access to the workshop organization and tenant and guides you through signing in.

Trainers: see Trainer Setup.

Confirm that you can:

✅ Sign in to UiPath Automation Cloud and open the workshop organization and tenant

✅ Open Test Manager and Orchestrator in that tenant

docs.title: Connect Studio and Delegate
docs.text:
1. Launch Studio and sign in to the workshop organization and tenant.

  2. Open UiPath Assistant → Preferences → Orchestrator connection, sign in with your UiPath account, and select the workshop tenant.

    Assistant already shows you signed in and connected?
    1. Click Sign out. Your default browser opens and asks if you want to log out. Don't click it.
    2. In that browser, sign in to the workshop tenant.
    3. Go back to Assistant, click Sign in, and follow step 2.

  3. Select Delegate in the top ribbon. It shows only once Assistant is connected.

  4. Click + New in the left panel to start your session. Use this one session for the whole workshop.

Check it

✅ Studio shows you signed in to the workshop tenant.

✅ Home → New Project lists Test Automation. No Test Automation option? Ask your trainer to check your license.

✅ The UiPath extension is enabled in your browser.

✅ Delegate opens from Assistant's top ribbon.

docs.title: Set up Delegate
docs.text:
UiPath Delegate is UiPath's productivity agent, and the evolution of UiPath Assistant. You give it a task, and it completes the task end to end on your real machine, in your browsers and desktop apps.

flowchart LR
    A["Delegate a task<br/>(prompt, voice, or recording)"] --> B["Delegate does it<br/>(web, desktop, files, systems)"]
    B --> C["Save it as a routine<br/>(re-run anytime)"]

For testing, Delegate is fully integrated with Test Manager, so you can hand it testing work across the whole cycle, from planning and authoring tests to running them and reporting on the results.

docs.title: Choose how much Delegate does on its own
docs.text:
Select Adaptive from the mode selector next to the chatbox (or Settings → Security) and turn Smart approvals on.

Approval mode What Delegate does Cautious Asks before every operation Adaptive (recommended) Auto-approves known safe operations, and asks before the rest. Smart approvals also approves what Delegate judges safe Full access Never asks — trusted environments only

docs.title: Check the connection
docs.text:
1. Ask Delegate:

    List the tenant I am connected to.

    Delegate asks to approve PowerShell?

    Running PowerShell is a high-risk tool, so Delegate asks even in Adaptive. Select Allow Run PowerShell for this session. Delegate then runs PowerShell without asking for the rest of your session.

    Delegate replies with your organization, tenant and user name. If the tenant isn't the workshop tenant, switch it as in the Assistant already shows you signed in and connected? tip, and ask again.

  2. Ask Delegate:

    Run uip login status.

    If it says you're not signed in, ask Delegate to run uip login, and sign in with your workshop account. Don't continue until the login status comes back clean.

Delegate acts on your behalf

It uses your UiPath account and permissions, and every action is logged in your name.

✅ Keep screen context on Default (the screen icon next to the chatbox), so Delegate sees only the apps attached to the chat.

✅ In Settings → Security → Blocked websites, quick-add Banking, Payments and Password Manager.

docs.title: Orchestrator folder and robot
docs.text:
Signing in to Automation Cloud lets you open Test Manager, but not run tests. Test Manager runs tests through Orchestrator, on a robot, in a folder. Your folder holds:

✅ Your permissions, which let you run tests in that folder

✅ Your machine, with a testing runtime, where the robot runs your tests

Trainer-led setup: your folder and machine

Do this with your trainer, before or at the start of the workshop, as they tell you.

Create your folder

  1. Create a personal folder, as your trainer guides you. You'll assign your machine to it.
  2. You get your permissions through a group your trainer sets up. You don't need to set them yourself.

  3. In the Enterprise setup, use Custom Windows credentials:

    ✅ Username: open a command prompt, run whoami, and enter exactly what it returns.

    ✅ Password: your Windows sign-in password. Sign in with a Windows Hello PIN? Set Credential type to Smart Card and enter the PIN as the password.

    ✅ No password, or not sure? Tell your trainer before the workshop.

    See Configuring robot accounts (username formats) and Using Entra ID users with MFA (Windows Hello PIN).

Workshop shortcut

Your own user runs the tests. In production, an admin assigns a dedicated robot account and a machine template to the folder.

Set up your machine and folder

  1. In Orchestrator, select Tenant (top left) → Machines, and search for your name.

  2. Edit your machine template. Under Runtime details, set App Testing or Testing to 1, whichever you see, and save.

  3. Still at the Tenant level, go to Folders and open your personal folder. In the Manage Access tab, check that your username is listed, with Attended, Unattended under Robot Type.

  4. Open the Machines tab, next to Manage Access. Click Manage Machines in Folder, select your machine, then click Update to add it to the folder.

Check it: in your folder, Machines lists your machine with 1 under App Testing or Testing.

Check it later: your robot setup is only proven when Test Manager runs a test on your machine. You do that in 7. Add Test Cases to the Smoke Test Set, once you have an automated, published test case. If the run fails to start or sign in, check the Windows username and password here.

Next → Introduction: Test Cloud & Test Manager

docs.title: Test Cloud & Test Manager
docs.text:
Use the import time

The project import in step 1 takes a few minutes. Start it first: download and import the project, then come back and read this page while it runs.

docs.title: What is Test Cloud?
docs.text:
Test Cloud is UiPath's cloud platform for application testing. It brings together:

✅ Test Manager — plan, run, manage, and analyze testing

✅ Studio — build and automate test cases

✅ Orchestrator — run test automation at scale

✅ App Test Robot — the robot that runs your automated test cases

✅ Agentic Testing — AI agents, such as Autopilot for Testers and Delegate, at every step

docs.title: What is Test Manager?
docs.text: Test Manager links requirements to test cases, test sets, and results, so you always know what's tested and what's failing.

docs.title: Autopilot for Testers
docs.text:
AI agents built into Test Manager and Studio. Today you'll use:

✅ Evaluate Requirement Quality — finds gaps in requirements, such as undefined thresholds and missing edge cases, and suggests fixes

✅ Generate Test Cases — generates test cases from requirements

✅ Autopilot for Testers in Studio — turns a manual test case into an automated one, low-code or coded (C#)

docs.title: Delegate for Test
docs.text:
Delegate connects to Test Manager through the Test Cloud plugin, which comes on with the QA / Testing work profile. It uses the uip CLI behind the scenes, so you just ask in plain language. Delegate can:

✅ Run manual tests on your desktop and publish the results to Test Manager

✅ Manage test cases, test sets, and executions

✅ Report on results, and triage failures

✅ Schedule recurring test runs as routines

Rule for today

Treat everything Autopilot and Delegate produce as a draft. Review generated test cases before you create them, and read what Delegate is about to write before you approve it.

That's enough theory — let's build.

Next → 01. Import and Link the Test Manager Project

docs.title: 1. Import and Link the Test Manager Project
docs.text: You start from a ready-made UiBank project: a requirement, test cases, a test set, results, and attachments.

docs.title: Download the project file
docs.text:
1. Download Agentic Testing Workshop - Sample Test Manager Project.zip.
  2. Unzip it. You'll import the .tmh file inside.

docs.title: Import it into Test Manager
docs.text:
1. Open Test Manager in the workshop tenant.
  2. On Projects, select Import Project and drop the .tmh file.
  3. Replace the Name and Prefix (project key) with your own, for example UiBank_AlexS and UIBAS, so your project is unique on the shared tenant.
  4. Clear the Include automation information for test cases box.
  5. Select Import.

Important

✅ Clear Include automation information for test cases before you select Import.

✅ The import takes 3–15 minutes. Refresh the page to check: the project card shows Import in progress… until it's done, then Created on.

docs.title: Link the project to your folder
docs.text:
To run tests automatically, Test Manager needs to know which Orchestrator folder to use: the personal folder you set up in Prerequisites.

It's your turn now!

In your Test Manager project, go to Project Settings, open the Automation tab, set Default Folder to your personal folder, and click Save.

Skipped this step?

Runs fail with HTTP 400: Please assign folder to project level before executing testcases.

Your folder isn't in the Default Folder list? You're not assigned to it. Ask your trainer.

docs.title: Check it with Delegate
docs.text:
Open Delegate and ask:

List the Test Manager projects created by me, with their details. If there's more than one, ask me which one to use for this workshop. Remember that project, and use it whenever I ask about my project in this session.

✅ Delegate lists the Test Manager projects you created, including the one you just imported. If you have more than one, it asks which one to use.

Next → 02. Evaluate Requirements

docs.title: 2. Evaluate Requirements
docs.text: Vague or incomplete requirements lead to gaps in testing. The Evaluate Requirement Quality built-in agent finds gaps in a requirement, such as undefined thresholds, ambiguous input formats, and missing edge cases or validation rules, and suggests fixes.

docs.title: Evaluate it with a built-in agent
docs.text:
1. Open Requirements → Submit Loan Request.
  2. Click Optimize Coverage, and choose Evaluate Quality.

  3. In Provide additional context → Add documents, select these project documents (marked P), so the agent checks the requirement against their rules:

    ✅ UiBank Regression Tests.xlsx — the 5 existing loan tests and their step style

    ✅ UiBank Security Guidelines.pdf — input validation rules for the form fields

    ✅ UiBank Accessibility Guidelines.docx — form labels, error messages and keyboard access

    Where do these documents come from?

    They're the project's attachments, under Dashboard → Attachments:

  4. On the next screen:

    1. Select a prompt: choose Multifaceted Audit.

      Editing prompts and adding your own

      The built-in prompts are editable, and you can add custom prompts of your own. Manage them in the Prompt Library, under Project Settings.

    2. Choose a model.

    3. Click Evaluate quality. The agent can take a minute or so. You can close the dialog while it works.

  5. Under Latest activity, click Quality enhancements to see the suggestions.

  6. Expand each suggestion. Select Add to Requirement for the ones you agree with. Its status changes from To do to In work, and its title and suggestion appear at the end of the description.

  7. Edit the requirement. Under each added title, replace the suggestion with the rule itself, using the exact text UiBank shows. Your changes save automatically.

    Sample: turn a suggestion into a rule

    Your suggestions may differ. This one says rejection rules are missing:

    Applying with its second example in UiBank gives the exact text for the rule:

    Applicants requesting $150,000 for 3 years with $400,000 income: Rejected with "You must be at least 18 years old for a loan and the loan must not exceed 100k."

  8. Set the status of each suggestion you used to Done, from its status drop-down.

Check it: each title you added has a rule under it, not the suggestion.

docs.title: Fix the requirement
docs.text:
The original acceptance criteria need the same check. Test cases are generated from the requirement's text, so its messages must match what UiBank shows. The requirement says what UiBank should do: match its wording, not its behaviour.

  1. In UiBank, go to Products → Loans → Apply For A Loan, apply with an age of 17, and note the message.
  2. Edit Submit Loan Request. In the under 18 rule only, replace "Not approved due to age." with that message, and save.
Make every rule measurable

Edit the acceptance criteria themselves so each rule is measurable, with exact boundaries, such as 18 and $100,000. 3. Generate Test Cases generates test cases from this text.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your requirement is clearer and more testable — ready for generating test cases.

Next → 03. Generate Test Cases

docs.title: 3. Generate Test Cases
docs.text: The Generate Test Cases built-in agent reads a requirement and proposes test cases with manual steps. It works from the requirement you improved in 2. Evaluate Requirements. You review the test cases before they're saved. The project already has 6 test cases on this requirement. Generate once to see how the agent writes manual steps. You don't have to keep what it proposes.

docs.title: Generate them with a built-in agent
docs.text:
1. Open the Submit Loan Request requirement.
  2. Click Optimize Coverage, and choose Generate Tests.

  3. In Provide additional context → Add documents, select:

    ✅ UiBank Regression Tests.xlsx — the 5 existing loan tests and their step style

    ✅ UiBank Security Guidelines.pdf — input validation rules for the form fields

    ✅ UiBank Accessibility Guidelines.docx — form labels, error messages and keyboard access

    Add documents or Leverage RAG? Add documents Leverage RAG What the agent reads The documents you select, in full Only the relevant passages from a Context Grounding index Best for Requirements whose rules live in a few known documents Requirements with ambiguous terms or abbreviations whose meaning is spread across many sources

    In this workshop, use Add documents.

    See About Autopilot chat.

  4. On the next screen:

    1. Select a prompt: choose Valid E2E Scenario Testing.

      Editing prompts and adding your own

      ✅ For this run only — edit the prompt right here.

      ✅ For the whole project — create new prompts or edit existing ones in the Prompt Library, under Project Settings.

    2. Below the prompt, add these instructions:

      Generate 5 test cases. Give every step one action and an expected result, and add preconditions and postconditions.

    3. Choose a model.

    4. Click Generate Tests. The agent can take a few minutes. You can close the dialog while it works.

  5. Under Latest activity, click Generated test cases to see the proposals.

  6. Expand each proposal and keep it only if it traces to one acceptance criterion, has one action per step, uses realistic data and expects what UiBank really shows. Otherwise sharpen the instructions and regenerate. Create the ones you want to keep.

    In production, turn on Testing Process Governance so a second reviewer signs off.

  7. Choose at least 3 test cases on the requirement to use for the rest of the workshop: new ones, existing ones, or a mix. Note their names. You automate them in 6. Automate and Publish the Test Cases.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
You've gone from a requirement to reviewed, linked test cases in minutes.

Next → 04. Run Manual Tests

docs.title: 4. Run Manual Tests
docs.text:
There are three ways to run a manual test case. Each records its results in Test Manager.

What it runs Who runs the steps Apps it can test Setup needed Delegate (used in this workshop) One test case Delegate, on your machine Web and desktop apps None Manual execution assistant A whole test set You Any None Run autonomously One test case Autopilot, on a robot Web apps A robot in the project's default folder (set up in Prerequisites)

See Executing manual tests.

Manual execution assistant

You run every test case in a test set yourself, one after another.

  1. Go to Test Sets, open UiBank Smoke Test Set, and select Execute → Manually.

    Allow pop-ups for Test Manager

    The manual execution assistant opens in a new window.

  2. If the test case has a precondition, the state the app must be in before the test, set up the app as it says.

  3. Perform each step, then select Set Passed or Set Failed (comment on failures).

  4. At any step, capture a screenshot or upload related files as attachments.

    Pass several steps at once

    Select Set Passed Until Here.

  5. If the test case has a postcondition, the state the app must be in after the test, check it. Select Condition Met if it holds.

  6. Select Next to run the next test case. After the last one, select Done.
  7. Check the results in the project's Execution section.

See Executing test sets manually.

Run autonomously

Autonomous Test Execution runs one manual test case with Autopilot, in one click, on a robot. You start it from the test case, not from a test set.

  1. Go to Test Cases, open a manual test case, and go to the Manual Steps tab. In the right-hand panel, select Run Autonomously.

  2. Enter the Target Application URL, https://uibank.uipath.com. Run stays disabled until you do. Turn on Live Streaming to watch Autopilot drive the browser, and take over if needed. Select an AI Model, or keep the default.

    Run still disabled? Open Configure and set Runtime type to your machine's runtime, App Testing or Testing.

  3. Select Run.

  4. When it finishes, open the execution:

    ✅ Logs — each step's result, expected behavior, and screenshots. Expand a step to see what Autopilot did.

    ✅ Execution Log — Autopilot's reasoning, such as how it found an element or compared a result.

See Running Autonomous Test Execution.

No test case yet? Explore the requirement autonomously

Autonomous Exploration is exploratory testing with Autopilot: it learns the app, designs tests, and runs them within a time-box.

  1. Open a requirement → Autonomous Exploration.
  2. Enter the app URL, set a time-box, and select an AI model. Enable Live Streaming to watch it explore.
  3. Select Start. When it's Completed, select Show report.

Needs a Windows robot in the project's default folder (set up in Prerequisites), with the UiPath browser extension set to Allow in Incognito. See Running Autonomous Exploration.

docs.title: Run manual tests with Delegate
docs.text:
With Delegate, you can run a test case or create a new one from a business document. You review the work and decide what to save in Test Manager.

Go back to your Delegate session.

docs.title: 1 — Run a test case
docs.text:
It's your turn now!

  1. Keep only one UiBank tab open. Delegate finds the window by its title, and the prompt names UiBank.

  2. Replace <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY> with the key of one of the test cases you chose in 3. Generate Test Cases. A key is your project prefix, a colon and a number, for example UIBAS:43. Then paste:

    Run the manual test case <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY>. Open UiBank at https://uibank.uipath.com, follow the test case's manual steps in the browser, and check every expected result. Take a screenshot at the final validation step and save it to my Desktop. Push the results to Test Manager. If any step failed, explain the reason.

    It takes about 10 minutes. Delegate uses your mouse and keyboard, so don't touch them until it reports back. Follow its progress in the task list. If your screen locks, unlock it, and Delegate carries on.

  3. If Delegate asks for permission to push the result, approve it. It records the result in a test set execution, which you'll find under Execution.

  4. For any failure, decide: defect in UiBank, or problem with the test case?

Check it: Execution → open the execution named Delegate- followed by your test case name and the date. It shows the test case result and each step's result, with a Delegate trace file attached to every step, saved locally under Appdata.

Think about it

Did Delegate stumble on a step? Autopilot automates these same steps in 6. Automate and Publish the Test Cases, so fix them now:

Rewrite the steps of test case <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY> that were unclear during this run, so each one has a single clear action and expected result. Show me the changes before you save them to Test Manager.

docs.title: 2 — Create a new requirement and test case (optional)
docs.text:
The business has documented a new process, Loan lookup, in a Process Design Document (PDD). It isn't in your requirements yet.

It's your turn now!

  1. Download the PDD, Loan lookup process to be tested.docx.

  2. Attach it in Delegate, then paste:

    Analyze the attached PDD and create + save a requirement and a manual test case directly in UiPath Test Manager.

Requirement: Create one new requirement for the process described in the PDD (don't create it if an existing requirement already covers this exact process — check first and tell me if you find one instead of creating a duplicate). Name it Loan Lookup. Its description should summarize the user flow (pages/actions) and any acceptance criteria from the PDD.
Test case: Create one manual test case - infer name from the PDD, derived from the PDD's numbered steps/screenshots — one test step per documented UI action, each with an expected result. Don't use the loan ID shown in the PDD: the step that enters the loan ID should use a loan ID from a loan applied for today.
Final step: After the PDD's last action, add a step that verifies the loan details page shows the same loan ID that was entered, along with the rest of the loan's details.
Link: Link the new test case to the new requirement.
Report back: give me the created requirement key and test case key when done.

  3. Ask Delegate to apply for a loan in UiBank to get a new loan ID, then run the new test case with it.

Check it: a new Loan Lookup requirement, with a linked test case that has manual steps and a result in Execution.

Not quite right? Talk to Delegate

Open the new requirement and test case in Test Manager. Check the title, description, acceptance criteria, steps, and expected results.

Then tell Delegate what to fix, in your own words, just as you'd tell a colleague. For example:

✅ "The test case must check that the loan ID is the same, and that the loan's other details are displayed"

✅ "Don't use the data from the PDD in the test case"

✅ "Add the label 'Delegate' to this test case and requirement"

Keep going until you're happy with both.

Go further — Organize test cases in bulk

  1. Replace <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY> with the key of the test case you ran in part 1, then paste:

    Add the label "Delegate" to test case <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY> and to the Loan Lookup test case you created.

  2. Create a Test Tier custom field and set it on the labeled test cases:

    Create a custom field definition for test cases in my project:
- Name: Test Tier
- Description: How often this test should run: every build, daily, or before release.
- Object type: Test Cases
- Data type: Label
- Suggested values: Smoke, Core, Extended

Then, for every test case with the label "Delegate", set Test Tier to "Smoke".

Check it: open a labeled test case. Its Details tab shows the Test Tier dropdown set to Smoke (not a second Test Tier line).

Test Tier is only a field. It doesn't add test cases to UiBank Smoke Test Set.

Beyond running tests — Delegate across the whole manual testing cycle

Ideas to try on your own project, in your own words:

✅ Find test ideas — from a requirement's acceptance criteria, or from a screenshot of a screen, including boundary and negative cases.

✅ Write the steps — turn those ideas into manual test cases and link them to the requirement.

✅ Run them with you — Delegate runs the steps and stops to ask when it needs a decision from you. Don't paste passwords into the chat: keep test logins in an Orchestrator Credential asset and give Delegate the asset name.

✅ Record the results — create test results with screenshots of failed steps, and upload them to Test Manager.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your test cases are proven against the real application, with results in Test Manager. Next, you'll connect Studio to automate them.

Next → 05. Set Up Studio and Build the Object Repository

docs.title: 5. Set Up Studio and Build the Object Repository
docs.text:
Set up a Studio Test Automation project with Delegate, link it to Test Manager, and build the Object Repository that Autopilot uses in the next step.

Access required

You need an App Test Developer license to create and publish Test Automation projects.

docs.title: What you'll do
docs.text:
Delegate

You work in Delegate on this page: paste each prompt, then wait and watch it build in Studio. Click a step to jump to it.

Delegate Create a Test Automation project Install the UI Automation package Link Studio to your Test Manager project Build the Object Repository

docs.title: Create a Test Automation project
docs.text:
Delegate

Replace <YOUR_NAME> with your name, for example AlexS, so your package is unique on the shared tenant. Then paste:

Create a blank Studio Test Automation project named <YOUR_NAME>_UiBank Tests, with Windows compatibility and VB as the language, in Documents\UiPath.

Check it: Delegate reports the project in Documents\UiPath\<YOUR_NAME>_UiBank Tests. It works in the background, so Studio doesn't open the project yet. It opens when you link it to Test Manager.

Do it by hand in Studio

  1. In Studio, go to Home → New Project → Test Automation.

  2. Name it <YOUR_NAME>_UiBank Tests, choose Windows compatibility, and create the project.

docs.title: Install the UI Automation package
docs.text:
Delegate

Install the latest stable UI Automation activities package in <YOUR_NAME>_UiBank Tests.

Check it: Delegate reports that UiPath.UIAutomation.Activities is installed. Once the project opens in Studio in the next section, Manage Packages → Project Dependencies lists it.

Do it by hand in Studio

  1. Select Manage Packages in the Studio ribbon.

  2. Select All Packages and search for UiPath.UIAutomation.Activities.

  3. Select UiPath.UIAutomation.Activities, install the latest stable version, and select Save.

docs.title: Link Studio to your Test Manager project
docs.text:
Delegate

Paste:

Connect this project to my Test Manager project, then open Test Explorer to show its test cases.

Check it: in Test Manager Settings, the status is Connected and Default Project is your project. Test Explorer lists your test cases.

Do it by hand in Studio

  1. Select Test Manager in the Studio ribbon.

  2. Select Test Manager Settings.

  3. Check that the URL is your tenant's Test Manager, and select Connect. The status changes to Connected.

  4. In Default Project, type your project key and select your project from the list.

  5. Select OK.

docs.title: Build the Object Repository
docs.text:
Delegate

The Object Repository stores the app's screens and UI elements for every test case to reuse.

Building it by hand is usually one of the slowest parts of test automation: you capture every screen and element yourself. Tell Delegate what to capture, and it builds the repository for you. To cover every screen and element the test cases need, use the prompt below.

This prompt is built for Chrome

Using Edge? Before you send the prompt, change Chrome to Edge in the two highlighted lines:

✅ The first sentence: running in Chrome

✅ Under Application: Browser: Chrome

Keep the name UiPath Banking App, so the next steps still match.

Delegate

  1. Prompt in Delegate:

    Create an Object Repository in UiPath Studio Desktop for the UiBank web app running in Chrome.

Application
- Name: UiPath Banking App
- Browser: Chrome
- Capture each element live in the browser
- Prefer stable selectors (id, name, aria-label, visible text) over index-based ones
- Avoid dynamic values in selectors
- Name each element exactly as listed below

Screens and elements

1. Screen: Home (https://uibank.uipath.com/welcome)
   - Username (input)
   - Password (input)
   - Sign In (button)
   - Products (dropdown menu)
   - Loans (menu item in the Products dropdown; open Products first so Loans is visible when you capture it)

2. Screen: Selection (https://uibank.uipath.com/loans)
   - Apply For A Loan (button; the one on the Loans page, not the Apply For Loan button on the Welcome page)
   - Already Have A Loan? (button)

3. Screen: Form (https://uibank.uipath.com/loans/apply)
   - Email (input)
   - Amount (input)
   - Term (dropdown)
   - Income (input)
   - Age (input)
   - Submit (button)

4. Screen: Quote (the results view shown after you submit the loan application)
   - Result Text: the full text block of the response
   - Rate: only the number shown below "With a fantastic rate of:", without the "%" sign
   - Loan ID: the value shown below "Your new loan ID is:"
   Anchor these elements to their label text, not to the changing values, so the selectors work for any result.
   To reach this screen, submit the form with sample valid values. Save the Loan ID for screen 6.

5. Screen: Loan Lookup (https://uibank.uipath.com/loans/lookup)
   - Loan ID (input)
   - Retrieve Loan Details (button)

6. Screen: Loan Lookup Result (the results view shown after you look up a Loan ID)
   - Result Text: the full text block of the response
   - Loan ID: the value shown beside its label, anchored to the label text
   To reach this screen, look up the Loan ID you saved from screen 4.

Acceptance criteria
- All 6 screens and 20 elements exist under UiPath Banking App, named as above
- Every selector validates (highlights the correct element) on its live screen
- Report any element you could not capture reliably, and why

  2. Don't use your desktop or browser while it captures, except to approve Delegate's requests. It asks before it submits the sample loan application. If your screen locks, unlock it, and Delegate carries on.

The prompt also captures Username, Password and Sign In. If a test signs in, read the login from a Credential asset with Get Credential.

Write your own Object Repository prompt

Describe what you need in plain language, such as the app, its screens, and the elements to capture. Delegate can also review and fine-tune your prompt, or fix it when something's missed.

Check it

  1. In Studio's Object Repository panel, expand UiPath Banking App. It lists all 6 screens and their elements. If it's empty, reload the project.

  2. Open UiBank in your browser on the Home screen. Right-click an element, such as Username, and select Highlight.

  3. In the browser, the element is outlined in green, and its label anchor in blue. Repeat for a few elements on each screen.

If an element doesn't highlight, ask Delegate to recapture it.

Backup: import a ready-made Object Repository
  1. On your Desktop, create a folder named Custom Library.

  2. Download the library for your browser and move it into Custom Library:

    ✅ Chrome: UiBankORForChrome.1.0.1.nupkg

    ✅ Edge: UiBankORForEdge.1.0.1.nupkg

  3. In Studio, click Manage Packages from the top ribbon.

  4. Go to Settings.
  5. In Name, enter a unique name for the package source.

  6. Next to Source, click the ellipsis (...), browse to Desktop\Custom Library, and click Add.

  7. Select the new source in the left panel, select UiBankORForChrome or UiBankORForEdge, click Install, then click Save.

In the Object Repository panel, find it under UI Libraries → UiBankORForChrome (or UiBankORForEdge) → UiPath Banking App.

Complete this step before you continue

Autopilot for Testers builds your test cases from the Object Repository elements. Without them, it can't automate the test cases in the next step.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your project is set up, linked to Test Manager, and the Object Repository is built. This is a good point for a break.

Next → 06. Automate and Publish the Test Cases

docs.title: 6. Automate and Publish the Test Cases
docs.text:
Turn your manual test cases into automations with Autopilot for Testers in Studio, then publish them with Delegate. Each automation stays linked to its test case in Test Manager.

Before you start

✅ Your Studio project is linked to Test Manager, and the UiPath Banking App Object Repository is built, from 5. Set Up Studio and Build the Object Repository.

docs.title: What you'll do
docs.text:
You switch between two tools on this page. Each step is labelled with the one it uses:

Tool What you do Studio Desktop Work in Studio Desktop yourself, with Autopilot for Testers Delegate Paste the prompt in Delegate, then wait and watch it work in Studio

Click a step to jump to it.

Studio Desktop Automate the test cases with Autopilot Attach test data Delegate Publish the test cases

docs.title: Automate the test cases with Studio Desktop
docs.text:
Studio Desktop

Automate every test case you chose in 3. Generate Test Cases, 3 or more. In 7. Add Test Cases to the Smoke Test Set, you add them to UiBank Smoke Test Set, which runs them in 8. Run, Triage, and Report.

  1. In Test Explorer, right-click one of these test cases → Generate Test Case with Autopilot.

  2. Review it like a pull request.

    Review checklist

    ✅ One verification for the expected result

    ✅ Object Repository elements only

    ✅ No fixed Delay activities

    ✅ No empty or extra activities

    If something's off, ask Delegate to fix it, or fix it yourself.

    Best practice: structure each test case in Given / When / Then sections.

  3. Check the Use Application/Browser cards. Each test run should open a fresh instance of the app and close it at the end, so runs don't affect each other. This includes each data row in the next section. Your requirement and test case may not say so.

    ✅ First card: set Open to Always.

    ✅ Last card: set Close to Always.

    ✅ Cards in between: keep Open and Close as Never.

    Select a card, then set Open and Close under Properties → Options. Here, the first card opens the app and leaves it open:

  4. Run it locally.

  5. Repeat steps 1–4 for each of your other chosen test cases, so all 3 or more are automated with Autopilot.

Check it: each test case passes locally.

Optional: Fix the activity display names

Autopilot names each activity after its manual step, including the test data, which makes long, hard-to-read display names.

  1. Replace Submit Short-Term Request with the name of the test case you generated, then paste in Delegate:

    I've created test case Submit Short-Term Request using autopilot feature in Studio. Fix the Display names. Provide appropriate names.

  2. Reload the test case in Studio and check the new names.

docs.title: Attach test data
docs.text:
Studio Desktop

Next, you attach test data to one of the test cases you automated, so it runs once for each set of values in the UiBankTestData entity.

One row expects the loan to be rejected, but UiBank approves it, so this test case fails. Leave it failing: in 8. Run, Triage, and Report, you find out whether the problem is in UiBank or in the test.

  1. In Test Explorer, right-click one of your automated test cases, and select Add Test Data.
  2. Choose Data Service, and link the UiBankTestData entity.
  3. Map the workflow arguments to the entity fields.
  4. Add a Verify activity to compare the actual outcome with ExpectedOutcome.
  5. Run the test case and check that it runs once for each data variation, and fails on the row with ExpectedOutcome set to FALSE.

docs.title: Publish the test cases
docs.text:
Delegate

Switch back to Delegate

Your test cases are automated. Go back to Delegate to publish them.

Replace <TEST_CASE_1>, <TEST_CASE_2>, <TEST_CASE_3> with the names of the test cases you automated (add more if you have them), then paste:

Set the test cases I generated with Autopilot in <YOUR_NAME>_UiBank Tests (<TEST_CASE_1>, <TEST_CASE_2>, <TEST_CASE_3>) as publishable, and publish the project to the Orchestrator Tenant Processes Feed, not my Personal Workspace.
Do it by hand in Studio

  1. In the Project panel, right-click each automated test case → Set as Publishable.

  2. Select Publish in the Studio ribbon.

  3. In Publish Test Cases, check the Package Name and New Version, then select Next.

  4. In Publish options, choose the Orchestrator Tenant Processes Feed, then select Publish.

Check it: in Test Manager, open Test Cases. Each one you automated shows as Automated. Open one and check that its Automation tab shows your package, named after your project.

Don't continue until every test case you chose is automated

The test set runs only automated test cases. A test case you chose that isn't linked to your automation is left out of the run and the report.

Replace <TEST_CASE_1>, <TEST_CASE_2>, <TEST_CASE_3> as before, then paste in Delegate:

For each of these test cases in my Test Manager project: <TEST_CASE_1>, <TEST_CASE_2>, <TEST_CASE_3>, tell me whether it's linked to a Studio project named '<YOUR_NAME>_UiBank Tests'. List the ones that aren't.

Automate any test case on that list, publish again, then ask again. Continue only when the list is empty.

Automated in Studio, but still not linked?

Ask Delegate to link it:

Link the automation <STUDIO_TEST_CASE> in my <YOUR_NAME>_UiBank Tests package to test case <TEST_CASE_KEY> in my Test Manager project.

Or, in Test Manager, open the test case → Automation tab → Select Automation.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your test cases are automated, data-driven, and published, ready to run from Test Manager.

Next → 07. Add Test Cases to the Smoke Test Set

docs.title: 7. Add Test Cases to the Smoke Test Set
docs.text: A test set groups test cases that run together. Your project already has one: UiBank Smoke Test Set, with the existing loan test cases. Add the new test cases you automated, so the set runs them too.

docs.title: Add your test cases
docs.text:
1. In Test Manager, go to Test Sets and open UiBank Smoke Test Set.

  2. Go to the Test Cases tab.

    Static or Dynamic Assignment?

    A test set gets its test cases in one of two ways:

    ✅ Static Assignment — pick test cases one by one. The set always runs exactly these.

    ✅ Dynamic Assignment — add labels. The set includes every test case with at least one of them.

  3. Click Add Test Cases to see all the test cases in the project.

  4. Select each new test case you automated in 6. Automate and Publish the Test Cases, and add them. Existing test cases you chose are already in the set.

docs.title: Configure the automation
docs.text:
1. On the Test Cases tab, click Configure Automation.
  2. Check that the execution is set to your personal folder, the one you set as Default Folder in 1. Import and Link the Test Manager Project.
  3. Set Runtime Type to the runtime you set on your machine: App Testing or Testing. The panel shows 1 Runtimes Available, 1 Connected.
  4. Under Automation Packages, select Autoselect Packages. Check that it lists your <YOUR_NAME>_UiBank Tests package, and click Save.

See Assigning test cases to test sets.

Check it: UiBank Smoke Test Set lists every test case you automated.

Do a test run

This is the first time Test Manager runs a test on your machine. It checks your robot setup from Prerequisites, not just the test set, so a problem shows up here, not in step 8.

Open the test set → Execute → Automated, then check Execution. Every test case you automated should have a result. A failure is fine — you triage it in step 8.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Everything is in place to run, triage, and report.

Next → 08. Run, Triage, and Report

docs.title: 8. Run, Triage, and Report
docs.text:
It's release night, and the release manager wants to know: can we ship? Run the test set, find out why anything failed, prove it, and write the go/no-go report.

Check these first

✅ Your robot is available — connected and not busy, in your Orchestrator folder.

✅ UiBank Smoke Test Set has your automated test cases, from 7. Add Test Cases to the Smoke Test Set.

docs.title: Run and triage
docs.text:
A failed test doesn't always mean a broken app: the test itself can be wrong. You made this call by hand in 4. Run Manual Tests. Now Delegate checks each failure against the requirement.

It's your turn now!

  1. Go back to your Delegate session.

  2. Paste:

    Trigger the UiBank Smoke Test Set of my project in Test Manager and wait for it to finish. Then, for this run only, not earlier executions:
- Give me the totals: passed, failed, none, and restricted.
- For each failed test case and data row, compare its input data and expected outcome with the acceptance criteria of the Submit Loan Request requirement. Classify it as a UiBank defect (the app breaks the requirement) or a test defect (the test expects the wrong result), and quote the criterion you used.
- List any manual test cases in the set separately as not run, not as failures.

  3. Approve Delegate's requests. The important one is the run itself, a real execution on your robot.

  4. Wait a few minutes while it runs the set and checks each failure.
Run a single test case instead 
Run test case <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY> in my project in Test Manager, wait for it to finish, and tell me whether it passed. If it failed, explain why.

Check it: compare Delegate's totals with Execution in Test Manager. Delegate can be wrong, so check its triage against the requirement yourself.

What you should find

✅ Your test case with test data, from 6. Automate and Publish the Test Cases, fails on the row with age 66. The requirement rejects applicants over 65, but UiBank approves them. That's a UiBank defect.

✅ Its other rows pass.

✅ Any other failure comes from your own test cases. Check how Delegate classified it.

Delegate calls the age-66 row a test defect? Ask it to check the row against the over-65 criterion, and share what happened in the workshop chat.

The age-66 row passed? See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Prove it
docs.text:
A defect report needs evidence a developer can reproduce. Delegate repeats the failed application in the browser.

It's your turn now!

  1. Keep only one UiBank tab open.

  2. Paste:

    Reproduce the UiBank defect in the browser. Open https://uibank.uipath.com, apply for a loan with the data from the failed row, and take a screenshot of the result. Note the loan ID. Then look up that loan ID on the Loan Lookup page, and take a screenshot. Save both screenshots on my Desktop.

  3. Approve Delegate's requests. Don't use your browser while it works.

Check it: UiBank approves the age-66 application and shows a loan ID, Loan Lookup finds that loan, and both screenshots are on your Desktop.

docs.title: Write the report
docs.text:
It's your turn now!

  1. Paste:

    Create a release manager report in PDF for this run, and save it on my Desktop. I need a go/no-go recommendation before tonight's sign-off meeting. Base it on UiBank defects only, and list test defects as follow-ups. Include the triage, and add the screenshots and loan ID as evidence for each UiBank defect.

  2. If Delegate asks where to save the report, choose your Desktop. Keep the default file name, and select Submit.

Delegate gives the path to the saved report and summarizes it in the chat. Always review its output before sharing. The report shows:

✅ Scope — the execution it covers

✅ Totals — passed, failed, none, and restricted

✅ Success rate

✅ Triage — each failure, whether it's a UiBank or a test defect, and the criterion it breaks

✅ Evidence — the screenshots and loan ID

✅ Recommendation — GO or NO-GO, and why

Check it: the right call is NO-GO, because UiBank breaks the age rule, not because of the success rate. Delegate recommends GO? Ask it why, against the over-65 criterion.

Saved as .md instead of PDF?

Ask Delegate:

Create a PDF of the report and save it on my Desktop.

Think about it

How did you know the failure was UiBank's, not the test's? Would the success rate alone have told you to stop the release? What does a developer need to fix it? How long would this take you by hand?

Optional: Draft the defect 
Draft a defect for the UiBank age defect: title, steps to reproduce, test data, expected and actual result, loan ID, and the screenshots. Save it on my Desktop.

In a real project, log it in your defect tracker.

docs.title: Schedule it as a routine
docs.text:
A report you run once is useful. One that arrives every morning is better. You don't need to set this up today, but here's how it works.

Save it as a routine. Once Delegate has run a task, you can ask it to save the task as a reusable routine. For example: "Save this run, triage, and report task as a routine called UiBank Release Report. Include my Test Manager project in the routine, so it works when it runs on a schedule." The routine appears under Routines in Delegate's left panel, ready to run again on demand.

Put it on a schedule. Under Scheduled routines, a Day / Week / Month calendar shows every routine with a time slot. New routines wait in the Not scheduled list below it. Drop one onto a time slot or set it to recur, for example weekdays at 8:00 AM.

Start from a ready-made routine. The Test Cloud plugin includes Summarize last night's execution of a test set, already waiting in the Not scheduled list.

The machine must be on

A scheduled routine runs only if the machine it runs on is powered on and signed in at the scheduled time.

A routine suits a personal report. For the test set run itself, schedule the test set in Test Manager so it runs on the unattended robot, or trigger it from your CI/CD pipeline. Let the routine only fetch and summarise the results.

docs.title: Go further
docs.text:
Stay in the same session — it remembers the run:

✅ "Summarize the failures in three bullet points I can paste into Slack."

✅ "Add a section to the report with recommended next steps for the developers."

✅ "Regenerate the same report for a Developer, with failure details and stack traces."

More ideas in More Prompts to Try.

Next → You did it!

docs.title: You did it!
docs.text:
Congratulations! You've completed the hands-on workshop. Today you:

✅ Imported the Test Manager project and linked it to your folder

✅ Evaluated a requirement and generated test cases with Autopilot for Testers

✅ Ran manual test cases and wrote new steps with Delegate

✅ Built the Object Repository with Delegate, and automated test cases with Autopilot in Studio

✅ Attached test data

✅ Published your automated test cases and added them to the smoke test set

✅ Triaged a failed run with Delegate, proved a real UiBank defect in the browser, and made the go/no-go call

Next → Troubleshooting & Next Steps

docs.title: Troubleshooting & Next Steps
docs.text: You've built the full flow, from requirements to a go/no-go report. This section helps you go further and get unstuck.

docs.title: What's inside
docs.text:
✅ More Prompts to Try — other everyday tasks you can hand to Delegate: standup summaries, coverage checks, rerunning failures, and more.

✅ Troubleshooting — fixes for the most common problems with setup, login, execution, and the report.

docs.title: Taking this to your team
docs.text:
✅ Approval mode: the workshop uses Adaptive; in regulated environments, set Cautious and lock it centrally.

✅ Secrets: test-app logins go in Orchestrator Credential assets, never in prompts, steps or workflows.

✅ Runs: schedule test sets in Test Manager or run them from CI/CD on a dedicated test machine.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
✅ Delegate for Testing

✅ Delegate operations for testing

✅ Test Manager documentation

Next → More Prompts to Try

docs.title: More Prompts to Try
docs.text: Try these in Delegate, in the same session, so it knows your project. Ask for outcomes, not commands.

docs.title: Morning standup brief
docs.text:
Summarize today's test runs in my project — how many passed, failed, had no result, or were restricted?

In daily use, ask for yesterday's runs instead.

docs.title: Coverage check before a release
docs.text: In my project, what percentage of requirements are covered by test cases, and which requirements have no test cases at all?

docs.title: Rerun only the failures
docs.text: Rerun only the failed test cases from the latest run of the UiBank Smoke Test Set in my project, as an automated run on my robot, and tell me whether they pass now.

docs.title: Flaky or recurring failures
docs.text: For the failed test cases in the latest run of the UiBank Smoke Test Set in my project, look at their last 10 results and tell me which ones are new regressions and which keep failing.

docs.title: Read-only exploration
docs.text:
List the test sets in my project and the test cases in each one. Don't change anything.

Prompts that write

Triggering runs or updating test cases changes Test Manager. Read each approval request before you approve it.

Next → Troubleshooting

docs.title: Delegate
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / fix Delegate isn't in UiPath Assistant's top ribbon Your Studio version may be too old. Install the latest STS version from Prerequisites, and ask your trainer to confirm your access. Delegate asks for approval on every step The approval mode is Cautious. In Settings → Security, switch it to Adaptive. Delegate still asks before high-impact actions, such as starting the run in step 8. That's expected. Delegate can't find your project Delegate is signed in to the wrong tenant. Ask Delegate "Run uip login status." to see which tenant it uses. If it's wrong, ask "Log me in with uip login." and sign in to the tenant from your trainer. Authentication failed or 401 Unauthorized Your uip sign-in has expired. Ask Delegate "Log me in with uip login." and sign in with your workshop account in the browser window that opens.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / fix "We weren't able to locate a matching loan ID" The loan ID doesn't exist in UiBank. In UiBank, go to Products → Loans → Apply For A Loan, submit an application, and use the new loan ID it shows. Publishing fails UiPath Assistant isn't connected to Orchestrator. Reconnect it, then publish the test cases again. Delegate can't start the test set run The test set has no automated test case. Publish the test cases again, then check that the set lists them in 7. Add Test Cases to the Smoke Test Set. HTTP 400: Please assign folder to project level before executing testcases. The project has no default folder. Complete 1. Import and Link the Test Manager Project. Test cases are skipped with no result They're manual — not linked to a published automation. Complete Publish the test cases and check each test case shows an automation. The run fails to start, or the robot can't sign in The Windows credentials in your folder setup don't match your machine. Check the username (run whoami) and password in Prerequisites. Signed in with a PIN or no password? Ask your trainer. The run stays pending or hangs The robot is busy or disconnected. In Orchestrator, check the machine in your folder is connected and has an App Testing or Testing runtime. The test case with test data passes on every row UiBank now rejects applicants over 65, so the age-66 row no longer fails. Step 8 has no UiBank defect to triage, so expect GO. Tell your trainer. Tests fail with "Cannot communicate with the browser" A robot-side problem with the UiPath browser extension, not a product defect. Check the extension is installed and enabled on the robot machine.

docs.title: Report
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause / fix You can't find the report Delegate shows the path when it finishes. If you chose Current working directory, the file is inside the Assistant install folder, which is hard to find. Ask Delegate "Create a PDF of the report and copy to my Downloads folder". The report numbers don't match Test Manager Make sure you're comparing the same execution. Ask Delegate which execution ID it used.

Still stuck?

Ask your trainer, or ask in Delegate — for example "Why did that last step fail, and how do I fix it?"

Back to Home
